explanation: The text says being included in the book suggested a business was an important part of the community, so being featured was helpful, or advantageous. Nothing in the text suggests being featured was risky, misleading, or unremarkable; in fact, the text implies the opposite of unremarkable.

The game was an underground protest against an authoritarian regime, so copies had to be shared secretly, which is what "surreptitiously" means. This also sets up the contrast with "Though": once secret, the game is now openly available online. "Disingenuously" (dishonestly) and "dispassionately" (without emotion) don't describe a secret distribution method.

Alice compares the sound of the snow to someone kissing the window, which describes a quiet, light, gentle sound. "Sensitive" describes a person or surface that reacts easily, and "bland" means dull or flavorless, neither of which fits a pleasant sound.

The poem moves through one nature image after another (wild rice, a lizard, geese, cranes, twilight, mist over sleeping marshes) to build a picture of a marsh at nightfall. It doesn't separate animals and then plants (A), since it mixes them throughout, and no person living there is mentioned (D).

Text 1 says Ludington has been widely celebrated with stamps, statues, and TV series, and Text 2 says she is "revered by Americans today," so both agree that many people admire her story. Text 2 doubts the ride happened at all, so it wouldn't agree that she was crucial to the war (A) or that her route is confirmed (B), and neither text says she wasn't real (C).

The underlined phrases compare each speaker to someone swinging a badly balanced axe whose strokes miss, a metaphor for trying hard to express an idea about art and failing to get it out clearly. That's why they then turn to their neighbors to rephrase what they said. The axe is figurative, so B's literal "physical effort" is wrong, and no specific artwork is discussed (A).

The word "though" contrasts the many studies of high altitude with studies of below-sea-level locations, so there must be a shortage of the latter; "paucity" means scarcity. "Profusion" means abundance, the opposite of what the contrast requires, and a "quarrel" or "verisimilitude" doesn't fit the idea that the gap inspired new research.

The first sentence claims Mitchell uses her album cover art to emphasize ideas in her music, and the rest of the text gives one example: the Van Gogh-style self-portrait on Turbulent Indigo that reinforces the title song. The text never discusses Mitchell's influence on others (B) or a difference between the two artists (C).

The poem balances hopeful images of renewal (new roads, fresh seeing, lives renewed) against the reminder that the same backs will bend and the same sad feet will drum, showing life's repeating cycle as both renewing and burdensome. The poem doesn't compare times of day for memorability (B), compare joy and sadness as frequencies (C), or contrast individuals with communities (D).

The relationship is described as mutually beneficial: the tree gives the fungus carbon, and the fungus gives something back by helping the tree absorb nitrogen. To give back in return is to reciprocate. "Retaliates" also means responding in kind, but only to something harmful, which doesn't fit a helpful exchange.

Wilde argues that the soul is unknowable and that even after measuring the sun, moon, and stars, the self remains a mystery. The rhetorical question, which expects the answer "no one," reinforces that doubt about truly knowing oneself. The text doesn't question the value of self-knowledge (B) or give directions for achieving it (C).

Text 1 claims public art that isn't bland provokes backlash, implying the art's own provocative qualities cause the reaction. The critics in Text 2 point out that similar art is received better in museums, so the setting and how the work is integrated into it also shape reactions. They would therefore say the backlash isn't caused only by the works themselves. They don't deny that unconventionality matters at all (A).

The text explains that the carte de visite made photography cheap, easy, and enjoyable for everyday people, so it helped make photography popular, or popularize it. "Praise" means to express approval, which isn't what an invention does, and "weaken" and "isolate" contradict the text.

The underlined portion is the first step of the route the geese usually take ("Generally it takes..."), so it describes part of their typical migration. The change in behavior is introduced only later with "In 2020, however," so it doesn't illustrate a change (A).

Despite critics' doubts, Whatley's determined advocacy succeeded, so the concerns didn't slow down or hinder his efforts. "Enhance" would mean the criticism improved his efforts, which doesn't fit the contrast set up by "Although."

The colon explains that the site is older than scholars thought when they first encountered it in 1911, so the new finding differs from the original, or first, estimate. "Genuine" would imply the old estimate was the true one, which contradicts the new finding.

The underlined portion states a common belief that happiness is always ideal, and the word "however" signals that research challenges it. Lench's finding that angry participants solved puzzles better calls that belief into question. The study wasn't designed to explain the tendency (A), and the belief isn't the basis of its hypothesis (B).

After saying a younger generation of musicians has embraced the album, the text names Blood Orange and Moses Sumney as artists who cite it as an influence, giving concrete examples. The sentence doesn't urge anyone to do anything (A) or mention criticism (B).

An overly permissive, mild nature would lead someone to tolerate or go along with others' bad behavior, which is what "indulge" means here. "Despise" and "criticize" are the opposite of permissive, and "moderate" (to restrain) wouldn't be a defect.

If the painting was made by a student under Vermeer's teaching, then Vermeer had pupils and wasn't working alone, which undoes, or negates, the view of him as a solitary artist. "Entrenching" and "substantiating" would mean the finding strengthens that view, the opposite of what's implied.

Critics prefer art that is cryptic or challenging, so Hannock's paintings must get little commentary because they seem the opposite: easy to understand and appreciate, or accessible. "Subversive" and "profound" are qualities that would likely attract critics' attention, not repel it.

The passage is a tribute to Faulkner, and anyone familiar with Faulkner would see the resemblance, so it must be a close copy, or imitation, of his style. "Rejection" contradicts Forrest's admiration, and an "opinion" wouldn't resemble a writing style.

The conclusion that Little Foot was adapted to tree life only makes sense if its bones were similar, or comparable, to those of climbing apes. "Independent of" would suggest no relationship, and the bones obviously weren't "obtained from" modern apes.

The play had "the opposite effect" of what the playwrights hoped, wearying audiences instead of energizing them, so they hoped it would be energizing, or rousing. None of the other words is the opposite of "wearying."
The photograph contained and showed a portrait of Rosita, so "featured" means displayed. A photo can't question, approve, or ignore its subject.

The whole text is about archaeologists' recent discovery of a food shop in Pompeii and what its contents reveal about daily life there. Artworks are mentioned only as items found at the site, not compared with modern art (A), and politics and climate are never discussed.

Many one-way trips move bicycles away from some locations and pile them up elsewhere. The sentence contrasts the blank with "other areas with insufficient supply," so the first group of locations must be emptied of bikes, or depleted of them. "Saturated with" is tempting, but it doesn't fit the logic of the sentence, which pairs "some locations" with "other areas" as two different problem spots.

Hull's team found that Deccan Traps gases did affect the climate but that conditions returned to normal well before the extinctions, which instead lined up with the asteroid impact. So they would reject the claim that volcanic climate change was the true cause. They never say the eruption caused the event (A) or that the impact caused the eruption (C).

The underlined phrase begins with "particularly at a time when" and explains why advertisers hesitated: new TV sets weren't being made during the war, so the size of the audience was uncertain. It doesn't describe what broadcasters did to persuade advertisers (C), and radio is mentioned only in the previous sentence (A).

The text explains Portland's deconstruction law, meant to reduce demolition waste, and then reports the 2019 study results (27 percent reused, the rest recycled). It never discusses popular support (B), argues against deconstruction (C), or compares Portland with other cities (D).

Because two of the century's greatest ballet dancers were Osage, ballet has a real connection to Osage history, making it a fitting, or suitable, way to tell Osage stories. "Arbitrary" and "unpredictable" suggest the choice had no good reason, which contradicts the "because" clause.

The colon introduces a detailed list of how each plant supports the others, showing a complex, interconnected system, which is what "intricate" means. The text explains the relationships clearly, so they aren't "indecipherable" or "obscure," and nothing suggests they are merely "ornamental."

Text 2 says there's no contemporary evidence that the audience panicked, and that the story persists because we strongly believe film was transformative. So Text 1's description is driven more by a sense of film's importance than by facts. Text 2 says historians accept the story, not that they find it naive (B), and it doesn't say early audiences found film alarming (D).

The phrase follows "When I started to talk on my own," and the author adds that she was "loud and unrelenting," so she means she talked constantly. Nothing in the text is about sitting still (A) or changing her mind (B), and her sister's friends could hardly stand her, so C doesn't fit.

The paradox is that water is essential to life's reactions yet, on the early ocean-covered Earth, it likely got in the way of forming biomolecules. "Hampered" (hindered) creates that contradiction. "Exploited" or "reflected" wouldn't produce a paradox at all.

The narrator says she hated the piano from the moment it arrived and describes it glaring at her like a caged bird, so the text establishes her negative feelings about it. She didn't want it near her bedroom (A), and the text says only that it was a Christmas gift, not what led to buying it (D).
Bell "worked closely with Woolf" to create the cover art, which describes a collaboration, or partnership. Nothing suggests a rebellion or disagreement between the sisters.

The painters "employ a range of styles," from traditional tribal arts to modernism to new blends. That variety disproves a misconception that Native art is all the same, or homogeneous. "Individualistic" would actually be consistent with a range of styles, so it isn't something this evidence disproves.

Cecily says one can put up with the absence of old friends calmly ("with equanimity"), in contrast to an "almost unbearable" separation from new acquaintances. So "endure" means tolerate. "Persist" means to last or continue, which doesn't take an object like "the absence."

The first four lines list ways people control nature (cultivating land, taming forests, irrigating deserts), and the rest says we must always leave the vast seashore alone, a reminder that some nature can't be controlled. The poem doesn't say such efforts are temporary (B) or call them admirable and then challenge them (C).

The example says people find blues and greens more appealing than yellows and oranges, so some colors are more attractive to viewers. Nothing in the example is about confusion, correction, or similarity.
The spacecraft was "gathering pieces" of the surface to bring back to Earth, which means it collected a sample. It didn't attach, follow, or replace the sample.

The underlined sentence explains the result of Brown's use of interviews: she gained valuable insights into her subjects' daily lives. That is how the oral histories benefited her book. The sentence says nothing about geography, politics, or a specific historical event.

Purists treat Bill Monroe's recordings as the pure folk standard, but Text 2 points out that Monroe himself created bluegrass by mixing folk with jazz and the blues. So the purists ignore how the genre actually began, which makes their position illogical. Text 2 says nothing about purists' own tastes (A), enforcement (B), or audience size (C).

Bremner claims Appia lacked technical expertise, but Text 2 says he was "not an amateur" and that as a young apprentice to a lighting specialist he observed hand-operated portable lighting. Text 2's author would therefore argue he gained real technical expertise there. The other choices raise topics Text 2 never mentions.

The dodder flowers "at the same time as" its host, so what it achieves is timing its flowering together with the host, which is synchronization. "Prediction" is tempting since the dodder senses an approaching event, but the word refers back to flowering at the same time, not to forecasting.

Text 1 says the moon formed from the debris "over the course of thousands of years," while Text 2 says it probably formed within a few hours of the impact. So Text 1 holds that the moon formed more slowly. Neither text discusses when the moon formed in Earth's history (A), evidence for Theia (B), or surface similarity (C).

Mrs. Wilkins stays where she is and extends her arm to the bowl of oranges, so "reaching across to" means stretching toward. "Arriving at" suggests she moved to the bowl, but the text says she stayed in place.

The text opens with the wolf's eradication in 1926, then describes the elk overpopulation and overgrazing that showed scientists how essential the wolf was, which explains why it was reintroduced in 1996. Only one solution is described, not several potential ones (A), and the text doesn't say why the park allowed the eradication (D).

The text opens by asking whether penguins were always flightless, and the underlined sentence answers it: Cole's team argues they once could fly but lost that ability. The next sentence supports this answer rather than being contradicted by it (B), and no term is defined (A).

Bursts from neutron star mergers usually last under 2 seconds, so one lasting 200 seconds is highly unusual, an oddity. "Incident" just means an event and doesn't capture how unusual it is, and "coincidence" and "reprieve" don't fit the contrast.

The example gives the first description of the seven-day week, showing that Sumerian civilization originated, or introduced, concepts still used today. "Inherited" would mean the Sumerians received these ideas from someone earlier, which contradicts "first."

Later scientists used Weber's key experiments as "the basis" for their own work, so his research laid the foundation, making it foundational. "Supplementary" would mean it merely added to others' work, and "ineffective" contradicts the text.

The text first gives Mukerjee's criticism that Eurocentric social science concepts didn't fit India, then shows his response: proposing the communalist "Indian village" as a model for policy. It never discusses his training or policies he oversaw (A) or his influence on other scientists (B).

The text walks through how Raccoon Mountain works: pumping water uphill when demand is low and letting it flow down through turbines when demand peaks. That explains the basics of one energy technology. It doesn't compare two methods (A) or urge utilities to act (C), and the facility dates from the 1970s, so it isn't new (D).

Sugimoto describes loving both countries and feeling as if she were looking down on "two separate worlds," then explains how she tried to make sense of puzzling American customs using Japanese standards. That conveys her experience of observing and interpreting differences between two cultures she embraces. She never mentions sharing customs with new friends (B) or hesitating to ask questions (C).

The new evidence shows silk was used outside China at least 1,000 years earlier than scholars believed, so it goes against, or contradicts, the old view. "Investigated" is too neutral, and "misinterpreted" would mean the evidence misread the view rather than disproved it.

The beads appear in large numbers at many sites across western North Africa, so the researchers are explaining why the beads seem to be everywhere, their ubiquity. The explanation (spread of symbolic behavior plus widespread shells) fits widespread presence. "Heterogeneity" means variety, which the text never describes, and "fecundity" means fertility.

The fern has the largest known genome, and because huge genomes are biologically costly, it's unlikely that any organism will have a larger one. To be replaced as the record holder is to be superseded. "Curtailed" (shortened) and "obviated" (made unnecessary) don't relate to the genome's status as the largest.

The text first describes Mitchell's idea that books for toddlers should mirror how they use language, through repetition and naming, and then presents Goodnight Moon as a book shaped by that idea. There's no debate between two authors (A) and no contrasting view (B).

The next sentence says she avoided "standard shapes and colors" in favor of innovative forms and daring hues, so she avoided traditional designs. "Creative" and "bold" describe what she embraced, not what she avoided.

The text says many animals use tools and gives examples beyond primates, such as dolphins using sponges and palm cockatoos using leaves, so its purpose is to show that a variety of animals use tools. It doesn't question bird intelligence (A) or compare cockatoos with humans (B).

"Indeed, Banisadr himself cites Bosch as an inspiration" supports the idea that Bosch's influence is real and worth noting, so recognizing it is "by no means unimportant." "However" then adds that Gilgamesh may matter even more. "By no means appropriate" would contradict Banisadr's own statement, and "substantial" and "satisfying" don't fit the sentence's logic.

Astronomers made a prediction based on calculations and models, and later observations confirmed it, so the blank refers to a theory. It wasn't "evidence" (the observations were the evidence) or an "experiment."

The women are testing the trees to see if sap appears, and the underlined sentence adds that the trees differ, like people, with some yielding sap readily and others reluctantly. It elaborates on the trait the women are evaluating. The "individual characters" belong to the trees, not the women (A).

The list of shared traits (spines, pointed snouts, small size) shows the two animals resemble each other, so tenrecs share similarities with true hedgehogs. The other choices don't make sense with the verb "share" and the list of common features.

Artemieva notes that iridium is common at the crater and in worldwide layers from the impact, and that long-period comets lack iridium while some asteroids are rich in it. So she would say Siraj's comet hypothesis fails to explain the iridium. She doesn't praise the hypothesis (C), and Text 2 never discusses how typical Wild 2 is (A).

The artworks are inaccessible because they need software like Adobe Flash, which was discontinued, so the software is no longer in use, or defunct. "Ubiquitous" (everywhere) is the opposite, and "arcane" (obscure) doesn't explain why the works can't be viewed at all.

Text 1's problem is that countries define urban settlements differently, making comparisons hard. Text 2 describes a new measure with global criteria for cities, towns, and rural areas, which directly addresses that problem, so its author would point to an available solution. Text 2 doesn't add more difficulties (C) or call for more investigation (A).

Anbar et al. read the Mo increase as a sign that atmospheric oxygen briefly rose 2.5 Ga. Slotznick et al. argue the Mo came from volcanic debris that was weathered by fluid seeping through microfractures "long after" deposition, so the Mo spike wouldn't reflect oxygen at that time. Both groups attribute the Mo to oxidative weathering (C), and neither denies the Mo increase is real (D).

The colon explains that the handcrafted materials and medieval-style ornamentation exemplify preindustrial artistry, so Morris's rejection of industrialization is clearly visible, or manifest, in these features. "Complicated by" would imply the features undercut his stance, which contradicts the explanation.

Because there are over 500,000 minor planets, the already hard job of giving each a unique name becomes nearly impossible to overcome, or insurmountable. That's why most just get numbers. "Feasible" contradicts this, and "unnecessary" doesn't follow from the large number of bodies.

Text 1 says Impressionists likely chose painted frames to set themselves apart from convention, and Text 2 says they chose frame colors to harmonize with their paintings. They disagree about the reason, but both say the painters chose frames deliberately. B reverses Text 2's point (frames matched paintings, not the other way around), and Text 1 says Degas was like many Impressionists (D).
The galleries are set up so every picture's name is plainly visible, so "arranged" means organized. "Ranked" would mean placing paintings in order of quality, which the text doesn't describe.

Elizabethan society laid down rigid gender expectations, later called "socially dictated" roles. Expectations that are set as rules are prescribed. "Illustrated" means shown or depicted, which doesn't capture society imposing the rules.

Hegel's prose is described as "frustratingly dense," something readers must work to "penetrate," so his works seem hard to understand, or opaque, at first glance. "Facile" (overly simple) is the opposite, and "authoritative" wouldn't create the contrast with "Despite."

Text 1 explains Moore's view that everyone, including philosophers, instinctively knows certain things, such as that they have bodies and live among three-dimensional objects, "whether or not they profess otherwise." So Text 1's author would say skeptics' doubt about the external world clashes with beliefs they can't help holding. Text 1 calls Moore's work groundbreaking, so it wouldn't call it unserious (A).
The exhibition includes works from González's great-grandfather down to her niece, so it covers, or spans, five generations. It doesn't borrow, judge, or neglect generations.

The underlined lines describe the waves as constantly pushed back yet always rushing forward again, filled with a life "that will not know defeat," which portrays them as relentless and enduring. The poem's tone is delighted, not intimidated (A) or uncertain (C).

The text describes researchers offering gift cards or other compensation to entice participants, so people join in response to an incentive, or inducement. "Appeasement" means giving in to demands to calm someone, which doesn't fit, and "propensity" (a tendency) isn't something offered to people.
